description: Introductory, non-scored catalogue. Not an exhaustive or validated classification.
exclusion_policy: Religion-centred ideological families are intentionally excluded; religious context may appear only where historically relevant.

records.name: Liberalism
records.summary: A family of traditions that gives central importance to individual liberty, equal civic standing, rights and justified political authority.
records.recurring_ideas: Civil liberties; constitutional limits; consent and accountability; pluralism; diverse views on markets and welfare.
records.internal_debates: Classical, social, egalitarian and other liberalisms differ on property, redistribution and the conditions needed for meaningful freedom.
records.classification_caution: Not synonymous with laissez-faire economics or any single contemporary party.

records.name: Conservatism
records.summary: A broad tradition emphasising continuity, inherited institutions, social practices and prudence in political change.
records.recurring_ideas: Institutional continuity; tradition; gradual reform; social order; scepticism toward abstract political redesign.
records.internal_debates: Burkean, traditionalist, national, religious, liberal-conservative and one-nation strands differ substantially.
records.classification_caution: Do not equate every conservative tradition with authoritarianism or reaction.

records.name: Socialism
records.summary: A diverse family of traditions critical of capitalist ownership and power, proposing greater social control, equality or cooperation in economic life.
records.recurring_ideas: Social ownership in varied forms; economic democracy; solidarity; reduction of class domination; debate over planning and markets.
records.internal_debates: Democratic, revolutionary, market, libertarian and state-centred socialisms differ on institutions and transition.
records.classification_caution: Socialism is not one uniform economic blueprint.

records.name: Social democracy
records.summary: A democratic tradition seeking to reconcile a market economy with social protection, redistribution, labour rights and public services.
records.recurring_ideas: Welfare state; collective bargaining; progressive taxation; public services; regulated markets; electoral democracy.
records.internal_debates: Historically includes both reformist socialism and post-war mixed-economy traditions; contemporary versions vary on privatisation and fiscal policy.
records.classification_caution: Not identical to democratic socialism, although the traditions overlap historically.

records.name: Democratic socialism
records.summary: A family of socialist approaches committed to democratic institutions and extending democracy into economic life.
records.recurring_ideas: Political pluralism; public or cooperative ownership in some sectors; workplace democracy; social equality.
records.internal_debates: Disagreements concern the role of markets, public ownership, planning and gradual versus transformative reform.
records.classification_caution: Do not use as a synonym for every welfare-state policy.

records.name: Marxism
records.summary: A tradition of social analysis and political critique drawing on Karl Marx and later interpreters, especially concerning class, capitalism and historical change.
records.recurring_ideas: Historical materialism; class relations; critique of capital; exploitation; emancipation; varied theories of state and revolution.
records.internal_debates: Marxist schools disagree on philosophy, strategy, democracy, party organisation and the interpretation of Marx.
records.classification_caution: Marxism is internally plural and is not interchangeable with the policies of any one state.

records.name: Marxism–Leninism
records.summary: A twentieth-century communist doctrine associated with Leninist party organisation and later codification in the Soviet state tradition.
records.recurring_ideas: Vanguard party; imperialism theory; revolutionary transition; planned economy; party-state institutions.
records.internal_debates: Its meaning and practice varied across states and movements; scholars distinguish doctrine from actual governing practice.
records.classification_caution: Record authoritarian rule, repression and historical outcomes separately from stated doctrine.

records.name: Maoism
records.summary: A revolutionary communist tradition associated with Mao Zedong, peasant mobilisation and protracted people's war, later adapted by movements beyond China.
records.recurring_ideas: Peasant-based revolution; mass line; people's war; continuing class struggle; revolutionary mobilisation.
records.internal_debates: Mao's policies and later Maoist movements differ by period and country; the Great Leap Forward and Cultural Revolution require explicit historical context.
records.classification_caution: Do not conflate all Chinese state policy after 1949 with Maoist doctrine.

records.name: Anarchism
records.summary: A family of theories sceptical of the legitimacy of coercive hierarchy and state authority, often advocating voluntary association and non-dominating social organisation.
records.recurring_ideas: Anti-authoritarianism; mutual aid; voluntary association; decentralisation; equality; direct action.
records.internal_debates: Individualist, collectivist, communist, syndicalist, feminist and other strands differ on property and organisation.
records.classification_caution: Anarchism does not simply mean disorder; distinguish philosophical theory from movements and tactics.

records.name: Libertarianism
records.summary: A family of views giving strong priority to individual liberty and limiting coercive state power.
records.recurring_ideas: Individual rights; freedom of association; limits on state power; property and voluntary exchange in many strands.
records.internal_debates: Right-libertarian and left-libertarian views differ on property, resources, markets and social equality.
records.classification_caution: Meanings differ across countries; do not assume the US usage is universal.

records.name: Nationalism
records.summary: A family of ideas that treats the nation as an important source of political identity, legitimacy or self-determination.
records.recurring_ideas: National self-determination; collective identity; sovereignty; solidarity; cultural or civic membership.
records.internal_debates: Civic, ethnic, anti-colonial, liberal, expansionist and state-building nationalisms differ in membership and political aims.
records.classification_caution: Nationalism can support liberation or exclusion; evaluate each movement in historical context.

records.name: Fascism
records.summary: An ultranationalist, authoritarian and revolutionary far-right family historically associated with dictatorship, political violence and suppression of pluralism.
records.recurring_ideas: Myth of national rebirth; leader-centred rule; mass mobilisation; hierarchy; militarism; political violence; anti-liberalism.
records.internal_debates: Historians debate definitions and national variants; Italian Fascism and German Nazism are related but not identical.
records.classification_caution: Describe critically and historically; never normalise or present as an ordinary democratic policy option.

records.name: Populism
records.summary: A contested political style or thin ideology that frames politics as a struggle between a virtuous people and a corrupt elite.
records.recurring_ideas: People-versus-elite framing; claims to represent popular sovereignty; anti-establishment rhetoric.
records.internal_debates: Can combine with left, right, nationalist, socialist or other programmes; scholars disagree whether it is ideology, strategy or discourse.
records.classification_caution: Do not treat populism as a complete economic or constitutional programme.

records.name: Republicanism
records.summary: A tradition concerned with civic self-government and freedom from domination through public institutions and citizen participation.
records.recurring_ideas: Non-domination; rule of law; civic virtue; mixed or accountable government; popular sovereignty.
records.internal_debates: Classical, civic-humanist, neo-Roman and contemporary republican theories differ on participation and institutional design.
records.classification_caution: Not synonymous with the modern Republican Party in the United States.

records.name: Feminist political thought
records.summary: A diverse body of thought analysing and challenging gendered power, inequality and exclusion in political, economic and social life.
records.recurring_ideas: Gender equality; bodily autonomy; representation; care; anti-violence; scrutiny of public/private power.
records.internal_debates: Liberal, socialist, radical, Black, postcolonial, intersectional and other approaches differ in analysis and strategy.
records.classification_caution: Feminism is plural; do not reduce it to a single policy position.

records.name: Green politics
records.summary: A family of political approaches that places ecological limits, sustainability and environmental justice at the centre of public policy.
records.recurring_ideas: Ecological sustainability; intergenerational justice; precaution; decentralisation; environmental democracy.
records.internal_debates: Eco-socialist, eco-liberal, deep-ecological and green-growth approaches disagree on markets, technology and growth.
records.classification_caution: Distinguish political green movements from environmental policy adopted by other traditions.

records.name: Decolonial and postcolonial political thought
records.summary: Approaches examining how colonial rule and its legacies shape power, knowledge, institutions, identity and global inequality.
records.recurring_ideas: Self-determination; critique of colonial knowledge and hierarchy; cultural and political agency; structural inequality.
records.internal_debates: Postcolonial and decolonial scholarship have distinct genealogies and should not be collapsed into one school.
records.classification_caution: Use specific authors and contexts; avoid treating the Global South as intellectually uniform.

records.name: Pan-Africanism
records.summary: A family of movements and ideas advocating solidarity, dignity and political cooperation among African peoples and the global African diaspora.
records.recurring_ideas: Anti-colonial solidarity; racial equality; self-determination; continental and diasporic cooperation.
records.internal_debates: Includes cultural, political, socialist, federalist and nationalist strands with different institutional visions.
records.classification_caution: Distinguish historical phases and continental from diasporic projects.

records.name: Peronism / Justicialism
records.summary: An Argentine political movement associated with Juan and Eva Perón, labour incorporation, social justice rhetoric and a strong national-popular political identity.
records.recurring_ideas: Labour organisation; social rights; economic nationalism; state mediation; political mobilisation.
records.internal_debates: Peronist coalitions have ranged across economic and political positions; governing practice changed across periods.
records.classification_caution: Treat as a historically specific movement, not a universal ideological template.

records.name: Gandhian political thought
records.summary: A body of political thought associated with Gandhi's anti-colonial strategy, non-violence, self-rule and decentralised social-economic ideals.
records.recurring_ideas: Satyagraha; ahimsa; swaraj; village self-government; trusteeship; constructive work.
records.internal_debates: Gandhi's views changed and contain tensions, including debates on caste, varna, industrialisation, gender and modern state institutions.
records.classification_caution: Represent his caste-related positions and historical changes accurately; do not sanitise contradictions.

records.name: Ambedkarite political thought
records.summary: A tradition drawing on B. R. Ambedkar's critique of caste hierarchy and arguments for social democracy, constitutional rights and substantive equality.
records.recurring_ideas: Annihilation of caste; liberty, equality and fraternity; constitutional morality; representation; social and economic democracy.
records.internal_debates: Later Ambedkarite movements interpret his legacy in varied ways; distinguish Ambedkar's own writings from later party programmes.
records.classification_caution: Do not reduce Ambedkarite thought to reservation policy alone.

records.name: Nehruvian political thought
records.summary: A tradition associated with Jawaharlal Nehru's democratic, secular and developmental vision, mixed economy, planning and non-alignment.
records.recurring_ideas: Parliamentary democracy; secular constitutionalism; scientific temper; public sector and planning; non-alignment.
records.internal_debates: Nehru's ideas and policy practice evolved; later uses of 'Nehruvian' can refer to different combinations of these themes.
records.classification_caution: Separate Nehru's writings, Congress programmes and later interpretations.

records.name: Indian constitutional liberalism
records.summary: Liberal and constitutional strands in Indian political thought and practice, shaped by colonial, nationalist and radical reform traditions.
records.recurring_ideas: Rights; constitutional limits; equal citizenship; rule of law; representative government; group-differentiated rights debates.
records.internal_debates: Indian liberalism has multiple historical strands and has often combined individual rights with state-led reform and group protections.
records.classification_caution: Not a single party identity; include colonial context and critiques.

records.name: Indian Marxist and communist traditions
records.summary: A diverse set of Indian movements and intellectual traditions adapting Marxist analysis to colonialism, class, caste, agrarian relations and parliamentary politics.
records.recurring_ideas: Class analysis; labour and peasant organisation; anti-imperialism; land reform; debates on caste and class.
records.internal_debates: Includes parliamentary communist parties, revolutionary currents and independent Marxist scholarship with significant disagreements.
records.classification_caution: Do not conflate distinct parties, movements or periods.

records.name: Indian feminist and social-reform thought
records.summary: A broad field of Indian feminist, anti-caste and social-reform arguments addressing gender, education, labour, family, caste and political representation.
records.recurring_ideas: Gender justice; education; anti-violence; social equality; labour rights; critique of patriarchal institutions.
records.internal_debates: Includes liberal, socialist, anti-caste, Dalit, Adivasi, queer and other strands; not a single unified doctrine.
records.classification_caution: Avoid presenting upper-caste or urban reform histories as the whole field.

records.name: Indian anti-colonial nationalism
records.summary: A range of movements and ideas seeking an end to colonial rule and political self-determination in the Indian subcontinent.
records.recurring_ideas: Self-rule; mass mobilisation; constitutional reform and revolutionary action; plural and competing visions of nationhood.
records.internal_debates: Included constitutionalist, Gandhian, socialist, revolutionary, religiously inflected and other currents; their aims and methods differed.
records.classification_caution: Describe plural histories; this dataset intentionally excludes religion-centred ideological families as standalone entries.

records.name: Indian secular constitutionalism
records.summary: A constitutional approach to equal citizenship and state neutrality or principled engagement across religious communities, interpreted differently in Indian debates.
records.recurring_ideas: Equal citizenship; freedom of conscience; non-discrimination; constitutional rights; minority protections.
records.internal_debates: Indian secularism has multiple interpretations concerning state distance, reform and public religious practice.
records.classification_caution: This entry is constitutional-political, not a religion-centred ideology.
